To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the neuromuscular dynamic properties of tendon reflexes are quantitatively different in patients with stroke compared with nondisabled controls.

we developed a handheld instrumented tapping hammer to measure multiple quantitative measures of tendon reflexes in both patients with and without stroke and found that the tendon hyperreflexia was associated with the increased reflex gain, increased contraction rate, increased half relaxation rate, and decreased reflex threshold poststroke.

we developed a novel method to quantify neuromuscular properties of hyperactive tendon reflexes poststroke and demonstrated that the reflex excitability and contraction rate are higher while the contraction latency is shorter in patients with stroke compared with nondisabled controls.

the evaluation of neuromusculoskeletal dynamics in patients with stroke and the development of a novel instrument for the evaluation.
the evaluation of the neuromuscular dynamic of the tendon reflexes poststroke, which is an important aspect of the neurological state and motor function of patients poststroke.
the quantitative evaluation of neuromusculardynamics of tendon reflexes poststroke, which may provide insights for clinical evaluation, treatment, and rehabilitation of patients with stroke.

tendon reflex excitability is increased and the contraction dynamics are faster in patients with stroke compared with nondisabled individuals.
